subject: physics
title: Matter Waves
summary: Count photon bullets per second, tune an electron’s wavelength to a crystal and charge an X-ray tube to the right kilovolts.

chapter.name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

concepts: Photons per second from the power
learningOutcome: The student can find the photons per second from power and frequency, the de Broglie wavelength of an electron from the accelerating voltage, and the shortest X-ray wavelength from the tube voltage.

levels.title: Pixel’s photon count
levels.adds: Baseline: a beam of power P and frequency f delivers N = P/hf photons every second (Ex 11.4; Example 11.1).
hints: One photon has the energy E = hf, with h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s.
The power is the energy per second: P = N E, so N = P/(hf).
Mind the units: mW to W, and the frequency is in 10¹⁴ Hz.

levels.title: Eli’s tuning
levels.adds: New idea: an electron through V volts has λ = h/√(2meV), about 1.23 nm/√V, and matches a crystal when λ equals the spacing (Ex 11.10; Example 11.3).
hints: The kinetic energy is eV, so p = √(2m eV) and λ = h/p.
For an electron λ ≈ 1.23 nm divided by √V (V in volts).

levels.title: Charge’s power shot
levels.adds: Apply it: an electron that gives all of eV to one photon makes the shortest X-ray wavelength, λ_min = hc/eV (Ex 11.1).
hints: The most energetic photon takes all of the electron’s energy: eV = hc/λ_min.
With V in kilovolts, λ_min = 12.4 / V in Å.

misconceptions: Only light has a wavelength: a moving electron does not
The shortest X-ray wavelength depends on the target metal
A brighter laser means more energetic photons
